main_body: Half-timbered house with a large red tile hip/gable roof, plaster-and-timber walls, a door, a window and a brick chimney, plus a front gabled porch wing
top_band: Orange/red tile roof slopes with lighter highlighted tiles, rows ~0-42 at the main body, and a lit ridge cap at row 0-3; the gable roof of the front wing is also a visible slope
evidence: Down the middle the roof tiles form a large lit slope band, then a dark eave beam (rows ~42-45) shades the front wall below it. The wall is a plaster face with timber framing (rows ~45-74). The windows and doors are set between framing posts, and the front wing repeats the same roof-over-wall structure. The roof slopes are clearly visible surfaces, like the Beodeul house references, so this is a correct 3/4 building.

style.evidence: The roof has per-tile highlights, mid tones and dark gaps in about 5 steps, like the reference houses. The outlines are dark brown or red-brown beside wood and tiles, not black. The plaster has speckle, the timber has grain, and the window has a flower box, door studs and a chimney cap. Tile density is comparable to the references, and nothing looks flat or sticker-like.
